Additionally, we demonstrate empirically that the best schedule varies across programs, machines, and inputs.

papers.title: Device-Centric Cooperative Floor-Level Estimation under Sparse Anchor Deployment for Construction-Site Applications
papers.abstract: For construction-site applications in multi-story buildings, accurate floor-level estimation is important for tracking workers, equipment, and Internet of Things (IoT) devices. In buildings under construction, communication infrastructure and power-supply facilities are often limited and the indoor environment changes as construction progresses, making localization systems that rely on dense wireless infrastructure or fingerprint databases difficult to deploy and maintain. Low-power wide-area (LPWA) communication can provide wide-area coverage with a small number of temporarily deployed access points (APs), but under sparse AP deployment, AP-to-terminal observations alone may provide insufficient floor-related information for reliable floor-level estimation. To address this problem, this paper develops a device-centric cooperative floor-level estimation method that exploits inter-terminal observations as relative floor-difference information to complement AP-side information. For practical application with limited measurement data, AP-to-terminal observations are represented by an upper/lower-AP RSS contrast, while inter-terminal observations are statistically modeled according to floor-difference classes. The resulting AP-side and pairwise scores are combined in a weighted floor-label objective and approximately optimized using dual-order sequential iterated conditional modes (ICM). Ray-tracing simulations and LoRa measurement experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method under different AP deployments and terminal-selection limits.

papers.title: On Threshold Probabilities for the Stability of the Independence Number of a Random Subgraph
papers.abstract: For an arbitrary sequence of graphs $G_n$, we consider a random spanning subgraph $G_{n,p}$ in which each edge of the graph $G_n$ survives independently of the others with probability $p$. We obtain a general upper bound for the independence number $α(G_{n,p})$, from which, for an arbitrary probability $p=p(n)$, we derive sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability, i.e., for the equality $α(G_{n,p})=(1+o(1))α(G_n)$ asymptotically almost surely, as well as upper bounds for the independence number of the random subgraph, including unconditional ones; for $p=1/2$ they recover A. M. Raigorodskii's results of 2017 and 2026. Under additional conditions on the structure of the independent sets of the graph $G_n$, we find, up to a constant factor, the threshold probabilities for both asymptotic and exact stability (the equality $α(G_{n,p})=α(G_n)$). Special cases include results on the graphs $G(n,r,<s)$ for growing $r$ and $s$, including Kneser graphs for growing $r$; we also give examples of complete multipartite graphs, graphs on the blocks of Steiner systems, and $q$-analogues of Kneser graphs.

papers.title: Is 4-Bit Quantization More Than Noise to a Chat Model's Safety Behaviour? Attributing Behavioural Shifts with Matched Perturbations
papers.abstract: Chat models on phones and laptops are usually 4-bit copies of the model that was evaluated, and audits of such copies disagree about what quantization does to refusal. A 4-bit build is one of many weight perturbations of the same size, so a change in its behaviour could come from its specific rounding error or from any perturbation that large. In a pre-registered study of three 3-4B chat models, with paired tests, blind human labels and an 8-bit null, we find two 4-bit shifts of opposite sign: with a compliant reply prefilled, Qwen2.5-3B continues into harmful content more often, and on held-out jailbreaks Llama-3.2-3B complies 10.3 points less often. Matched perturbations separate the two. Shuffled and Gaussian versions of the error average close to zero, while scaling the real error, from its mirror image to twice its size, changes behaviour near-linearly. At half the real error, Llama's likelihood is almost unchanged, yet it already complies 5.8 points less often, and llama.cpp's Q4_K_M, at the same bits per weight, moves neither model. Refusal under 4-bit quantization depends on the specific rounding error, not on bits per weight or likelihood, so each build has to be compared with its original.

papers.title: Constitutive-fibre mechanics: mechanics-directed uncertainty in constitutive function space
papers.abstract: A structural prediction rests on constitutive functions that are known only through a finite number of tests. The tests fix the response along the states they visit; together with a declared regularity bound they leave a set of admissible constitutive functions, which we call the constitutive fibre. Constitutive-fibre mechanics (CFM) computes the range of a quantity of interest over this set. Adjoint solves of the mechanical problem represent the test observations and the quantity of interest as elements of the constitutive function space. The part of the sensitivity of the quantity of interest that is orthogonal to all observation sensitivities is hidden from the tests; for exact data it alone determines the half-width of the prediction, and for data with tolerance the half-width is a finite convex problem in the span of the adjoint representers. Comparing the two values shows whether a new type of test or a more precise test is needed, and a rank-one update ranks candidate tests before they are performed. A learned constitutive class can only under-represent the range; the deficit is computable. Beyond the linear range, an optimality system with state-dependent representers gives the extreme constitutive functions. The same set decides whether the prediction is defined for every admissible constitutive function, which is a different question from its precision. For a phase-field bar with unknown degradation function, 3% of the sensitivity of the stability eigenvalue is hidden and produces 70% of its uncertainty. For an open-hole composite lamina, the coupon that sharpens the compliance most is not the one that makes the prediction valid; validity is proved on a declared cell by a certificate accepted in exact arithmetic.

papers.title: From Imperfective Paradox to Moorean Absurdity: Single-Chain Reasoning Lock-In and Multi-Candidate Verbalization Across Aspectual and Pragmatic Ambiguity
papers.abstract: Natural language entailment and coherence judgments often depend on whether an event merely occurred, reached a telic culmination, satisfied a plan, or was evaluated under multiple pragmatic standards. We test observable consequences of the single-chain premature lock-in hypothesis across four preregistered, sealed formal experiments on Qwen3-8B-Q8_0 (16,640 formal units, temperature=0.0): 15 of 16 hypothesis slots retain confirmatory status (12 rejecting H0 under within-experiment Holm control at alpha_fam=0.05; E3_H3 demoted to descriptive status). In Experiment 1, Direct-CoT vs. MCU differs by 25.00 pp on telic high-confidence completion (Holm p=1.31239e-05), while NLI-CoT collapses by -91.25 pp on uninterrupted atelic items (Holm p=1.81805e-21). Multi-Candidate Verbalization (MCV) elicits K=5 weighted estimates in one call, separating the prompt from unweighted (MCU) and self-weighted (MCW) readouts. Mandarin (E2) and English (E3) expose an Interruption-Anchored Realis Paradox under NLI-CoT. In Experiment 4, MCU-CF raises perceived coherence on implicit Moorean sentences by 26.64 pp over Direct-CoT (Holm p=0.0006), alongside Direct-CF - Direct-CoT = 29.15 pp and MCU-CoT - Direct-CoT = 17.31 pp. A 1,800-call OpenAI ablation and a stage="dev" P16.7 cross-model extension (4,240 planned/collected units across five external models: 4,222 valid, 18 format-missing, 0 transport-missing; <2% missing per slice; OpenAI gpt-4o-mini at top_logprobs=20 achieves 1,000/1,000 valid units) show that discrete NLI-CoT and scalar Direct-CoT judgments dissociate across models. Confirmatory effects concern observable prompt-and-readout protocols; internal premature lock-in remains a hypothesis. All code, stimuli, preregistered analysis plans, and verification tools are available at https://github.com/asj252/llm-judgment-studies.

papers.title: SRED: Sparse Regional Evidence Distillation Across Magnifications in Whole-Slide Imaging
papers.abstract: In computational pathology, high-magnification whole-slide image analysis preserves tissue detail but requires encoding many patches, whereas lower magnification reduces computation by covering a higher field of view per patch while sacrificing detail. Existing cross-magnification distillation matches features that often encode detail unreachable by low-magnification input, sometimes requiring slide-level labels that limit scalability. To address those issues, we introduce Sparse Regional Evidence Distillation (SRED), which transfers regional event occurrences that encode reachable high-level interactions between details without slide-level labels. We use a sparse autoencoder (SAE) to learn an event dictionary from 20x teacher features. Logical OR pooling records whether each event is detected in any spatially aligned patch, retaining both localized and shared evidence within the corresponding 5x region. A pretrained 5x encoder is fine-tuned to predict these regional targets without slide-level labels. Visual analysis identifies dictionary components responsive to recognizable histological patterns, supporting target interpretation. Compared with native 5x features, SRED improves average macro-F1 by 1.1 points across seven classification and grading cohorts and average C-index by 1.7 points across five survival cohorts. Runtime matches native 5x, with an average 11.58x speedup over 20x.

papers.title: Emergence and Collapse of Leader-Follower Flocks through Phantom Targets: Surprise Nullification in Bayesian and Inverse Bayesian Inference
papers.abstract: In Bayesian and inverse Bayesian (BIB) inference, a large prediction error can trigger surprise nullification, which expands belief and likelihood variances by a common factor, leaving the updated variance ratio the same as in standard Bayesian updating. This can increase belief uncertainty while keeping the learning rate low. In the simulations, three agents used BIB inference to predict one another's positions and moved toward those predictions, repeatedly forming leader-follower flocks that subsequently collapsed despite having no alignment rules or designated leaders. Three leadership criteria (front position, heading stability, and flock initiation) identified the same agent in 89% of eligible flocks, with different agents serving as leaders across flocks. Flocks formed when an agent nearly stopped incorporating another's observations (link cut) and moved straight toward a predicted position detached from reality (phantom target), thereby attracting followers. Link cuts arose when two successive resets assigned a very small and then an ordinary likelihood variance, sharply increasing the likelihood-to-belief variance ratio. Flocks collapsed upon link recovery or when returning phantom targets balanced the leader's forward and backward attractions. Without nullification, cuts persisted throughout the analysis period; expanding only belief variance caused recovery within a few steps. Expanding likelihood variance as well allowed cuts to persist while belief uncertainty grew, enabling later resets and recovery. Thus, nullification preserves relative precision, allowing cuts and flocks to persist, while reducing absolute precision to enable recovery and collapse, reconciling these seemingly opposing processes through a single operation. These results suggest that, in this model, individually inaccurate predictions can give rise to collective order.

papers.title: RISA: Recoverable Sparse Attention for Block-Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Block-wise diffusion language models (DLMs) refine multiple tokens in parallel, offering an alternative to token-by-token autoregressive decoding. Their long-context inference, however, remains bottlenecked by memory-bound attention: every denoising step repeatedly reads a growing historical key--value (KV) cache. Directly applying sparse attention does not fully solve this problem, because different queries can select different pages, inflating the block's collective read set, while repeated support construction adds overhead and permanent eviction can discard information needed later. We present RISA, a recoverable sparse-attention method with shared read plans for block-wise DLMs. RISA exploits the fact that historical KV remains fixed within a block while queries evolve across denoising steps. Newly generated history is organized into exact priority and recovery tiers; seed queries then build a protected, bounded read plan whose indices are reused across the block while attention is recomputed with fresh queries and current-block KV. This separates history preservation from repeated reading and amortizes sparse-support construction without changing the backbone or decoder. On DreamReasoner-8B, RISA retains comparable task performance. At 32K, the default configuration speeds up attention by $2.67\times$ and fixed-trajectory requests by $1.36\times$ over dense, and attention speedup reaches $5.53\times$ at 128K. Across eight settings on three models, RISA decodes faster than the tested MAGE, QUEST, and LoSA budgets at matched KL.

papers.title: Symmetry-selected entanglement death at Floquet resonances of parametrically coupled qubits
papers.abstract: Periodic modulation of a qubit--qubit coupling is a standard way to engineer quantum interactions, but a strong modulation also reorganizes the transitions through which the qubits dissipate into a comb of Floquet channels. We study two identical, strongly coupled qubits whose transverse coupling is modulated anharmonically, as by a nonlinear coupler, with each qubit damped by its own reservoir. The modulation raises the ground-state concurrence of the cycle-averaged Hamiltonian from 0.45 to above 0.8, yet the steady-state concurrence stays close to its undriven value except at Floquet resonances selected by symmetry. There it undergoes entanglement death, vanishing at all times in the drive cycle over a finite range of modulation depths. Parity and exchange symmetry split the Floquet spectrum into an even sector, whose branches anticross at multiphoton resonances, and an exactly solvable odd sector, whose branches cross. Every dissipative channel connects the two sectors, so only the even anticrossings cause entanglement death, provided their gap exceeds the damping rate, whereas the nearby odd crossings leave the concurrence unchanged. Comparing time-independent and Floquet master equations, with and without the secular approximation, we show that the basis in which the dissipator is built changes the entanglement by up to 0.2 for an Ohmic bath and 0.5 for a flat one, whereas the secular approximation matters only near anticrossings with gaps comparable to the damping. The basis matters most when the bath has spectral weight at low frequency, where the drive moves dissipative channels through zero frequency. A transverse field that breaks parity lifts the selection rule.

papers.title: Stable recurrences of the super-transition array formalism from marked generating functions
papers.abstract: The conventional evaluation of super-transition-array (STA) mean energies and variances uses partition recurrences with alternating terms that can lose numerical accuracy. Here we apply a marked-generating-function approach to derive coupled coefficient recurrence relations that avoid these sums and directly accumulate fixed-occupation partition functions and arbitrary-order moments of the configuration-average (centroid) transition energies. Unlike explicit expansions into products of subshell occupations, the resulting recurrences require only one coefficient numerator per moment order. The same approach provides recurrences for polynomial occupation-number averages, which can be contracted to obtain the contributions of individual configurations to the STA variance and the Boltzmann energy correction entering the partition function. These contractions avoid the explicit evaluation of individual occupation-product averages and reduce the number of auxiliary quantities required. Numerical examples demonstrate agreement with direct configuration enumeration, including regimes where the alternating Bar--Shalom recurrences lose accuracy. Complementary hole-counting recurrences are also derived for all quantities, starting from a full supershell.

papers.title: Towards the componentwise three-soliton conjecture: cones, collisions, soft momenta and graphs
papers.abstract: The componentwise three-soliton conjecture of Part~I states that if an even polynomial $P$ with $P(0)=0$ satisfies Hirota's three-soliton condition on a non-hyperplane component of multiplicity one of its dispersion variety, then it satisfies the $N$-soliton condition there for every $N$. We prove restrictions on components carrying this condition and classify the polynomials satisfying it on several families of components, with no degree bound. Restrictions: if the top homogeneous part of the equation of the component has a nonlinear irreducible factor, then $P$ is a multiple of a quadratic form; the order of $P$ at the origin is tied to the multiplicities of the component and of the doubled component; a component through the origin has odd multiplicity; the condition passes to all limits of the rescaled component, and the Newton polygon of a plane component has edges of only ten directions. Classifications: on the cubic graph $v=u^3$, where the four-soliton condition holds exactly in multiplicity one; on the graphs $v=q(u)$ with $°q\ge3$, where $P$ exists only if $q$ is an odd cubic or an odd quintic, so the conjecture holds for all graphs of polynomials; and for three families of Hietarinta's list, where each irreducible member is, up to a constant factor, the only such polynomial on its dispersion variety. All three satisfy the $N$-soliton condition for every $N$, so the conjecture holds for them: two belong to the BKP hierarchy, and for Hietarinta's quartic equation, known to satisfy it for $N\le4$, we prove it by fusing resonant momenta and counting zeros on its curve. For translated hyperbolas we exclude the one through the origin and all $P$ of degree at most eight. The solutions of multiplicity one on graphs are known bilinear equations; new is that there are no others. The conjecture remains open.

papers.title: Haptic Probing for Subsurface-Aware Force Distribution on Layered Soft Tissue
papers.abstract: Force-regulated contact with layered soft tissue fails most often where the subsurface composition changes: controllers infer the substrate from the loading signal alone, so the estimate guiding them lags the change---more acutely, we argue, over compliant than over bone-backed tissue. We remove that lag with a separate haptic channel. Under a light preload, a brief low-amplitude excitation lets the local dynamic admittance discriminate muscle from bone-backed tissue relative to a per-subject baseline, before task force is applied---active haptic sensing used to commit a control decision rather than to characterise tissue. A force- and tactile-driven distribution law then consumes that regime throughout execution: an instantaneous allocation equalises pressure across the engaged fingertips, while the regime sets the admissible pressure and hence the area the hand must recruit to deliver the target force---making patch area a controlled variable rather than a by-product. Probing, switches and recruitment are priced in a partitioned passivity budget, so safety monitoring cannot suppress the probe and a refused recruitment forfeits force tracking rather than the pressure bound. We report force tracking and pressure uniformity over curved, migrating contact on three human subjects, with regime labels from anatomical landmarks.

papers.title: Microwave hinge states in an all-dielectric woodpile photonic crystal insulator
papers.abstract: Higher-order topological states are studied in a woodpile photonic crystal (PhC) having a large complete photonic bandgap. According to theoretical predictions, we fabricate a three-dimensional all-dielectric PhC with a millimeter-scale lattice period. The structure consists of two distinct lattice types that coincide through a structural displacement, where their interface intersection gives rise to hinge states. Microwave transmission measurements reveal transmission peaks and spatial localization at the intersection, demonstrating the hinge states. Furthermore, we confirm the absence of hinge states at a specific intersection. As theoretically predicted, hinge states emerge at intersections where the localized boundary polarizations are topologically different, whereas they are absent at intersections where the boundary polarizations are equivalent.

papers.title: Grid-Responsive Pricing of Dynamic Wireless Charging with Coupled Residential Demand
papers.abstract: Dynamic wireless charging (DWC) is an emerging technology that enables electric vehicles (EVs) to recharge while traveling. Its unique operational model creates two revenue streams for DWC operators through lane access tolls and electricity sales. However, these prices influence not only traffic flow and roadway energy delivery but also how much EV charging moves to homes instead, potentially within the same distribution network. Neglecting this coupling can underestimate grid loading and compromise pricing decisions. We develop a coupled traffic, EV energy, driver-response, and AC distribution network model with a model predictive control (MPC) framework that jointly optimizes DWC tolls and charging prices while explicitly accounting for displaced residential charging and network losses. Using 78 days of I-210 West traffic data, we show that conventional MPC exceeds feeder loading limits on 52 days, whereas the proposed residential load aware controller eliminates these violations with only 0.6% lower operator revenue. Under a more constrained feeder configuration, it eliminates 50 overloaded days with a 0.9% revenue reduction. Sensitivity analyses highlight the importance of accurate residential demand estimation and feeder loss modeling, while peak-aware pricing further reduces daily peak loading by 3.7% relative to the base load. These results demonstrate the value of coordinated pricing that captures the interaction between roadway and residential charging.

papers.title: Training Neural Networks to be Locally Adaptive
papers.abstract: Deep neural networks fitted by global empirical risk minimization commit to a single model for the entire covariate space. In a regression problem, if the regression function $f_0$ is inhomogeneous --- varying rapidly in one region, while being nearly flat in another --- no single model can be appropriate everywhere, and the fit degrades where the function varies most rapidly. Here we study an alternative in which, instead of fitting the network globally, we fit it locally. For each query point $x$, a \emph{local neural network} is trained on the $k$ nearest-neighbours of $x$ alone, making the training sample and the fitted function query-dependent. We analyze the performance of the resulting estimator through a localization approach, establishing that the pointwise risk of the estimator with an appropriate choice of $k$ attains the rate $n^{-2α/(2α+d^{*})}$, up to logarithmic factors, when $f_0$ is locally $α$-Hölder with $α\in(0,1]$ and the covariates are supported on a $d^{*}$-dimensional manifold embedded in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$. A matching Le Cam lower bound shows that this rate is pointwise minimax optimal. However, the local rate-optimality requires $k$ to be calibrated to the smoothness of $f_0$, which is unknown in practice. We therefore provide a locally adaptive choice of $k$ that makes the neural network adapt to the local Hölder exponent of $f_0$ and to the intrinsic dimension simultaneously, both of which are potentially varying over the covariate domain. An extensive simulation study demonstrates the dominance of the locally adaptive neural network over a globally trained network and several state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Observation of temporal routing of topological edge states
papers.abstract: The switching or routing of topological edge states is crucial for disorder-immune state transfer. Previous experimental observations have primarily relied on optical waveguide arrays that treat the spatial coordinate as an equivalent temporal dimension. However, direct experimental observation of the routing dynamics of topological edge states in physical time remains challenging. Here, we report the experimental observation of temporal routing of topological edge states. By constructing a lattice composed of two coupled nonlinear Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chains, the topological edge states exhibit temporal routing behavior controlled by nonlinearity. As the excitation voltage increases from the linear regime, we observe that the voltage intensity distribution transitions from periodic interchain exchange to slowed interchain exchange and ultimately to localization with strongly suppressed interchain exchange, thereby validating the phenomenon of temporal routing. These dynamics are experimentally observed within a finite time window limited by circuit dissipation. Our findings provide valuable insights into the temporal manipulation of topological edge states.

papers.title: MIRAGE: Motion Identity Reduction via Autoregressive Generative Encoding for Privacy-Preserving Skeleton-based Motion Data
papers.abstract: Skeleton motion identifies people through body proportions and movement style, and skeleton streams are increasingly passed to third-party analytics that run action classifiers trained on raw data. A prior adversarial anonymizer adds a per-frame residual in the raw coordinate space but sees one frame at a time; motion retargeting needs a target skeleton and complete sequences, which rules out online use. We present MIRAGE, a target-free, causal anonymizer that adds an identity-reducing residual to each incoming frame in the raw coordinate space, computed by attention over past frames. One causal, optionally windowed mask governs every attention in a rotary-position encoder-decoder, and key/value caches let the trained function run frame by frame; on all 56,578 NTU 60 sequences, batched and streaming outputs differ by at most 7.2e-6 m. Reported results use an unbounded window, so per-stream state grows with stream length. We evaluate against a passive adversary that applies raw-trained identity models and an adaptive adversary that trains on the anonymizer's output, treating the adaptive adversary as the headline, on NTU RGB+D 60 over five generator seeds, alongside the per-frame residual anonymizer of Moon et al. trained identically. When consumers retrain on the released data, MIRAGE keeps 83.9% action recognition (raw 89.1%; Moon et al. 88.7%) while a retrained identity classifier reaches 43.4% re-identification (RI) over 40 subjects, against 69.4% for Moon et al. and 75.4% on raw data. The strongest adaptive attacker still reaches 49.3% (chance 2.5%), so MIRAGE reduces identity leakage; it does not anonymize. Against raw-trained (frozen) classifiers, MIRAGE lowers RI below the strongest retargeting baseline (10.36% vs. 22.09%), but frozen action recognition falls to 37.04% (vs. 75.82%), so at full residual scale it is not a drop-in replacement for raw input to existing frozen models.

papers.title: Quality Control for the LGAD sensors of the ATLAS High Granularity Timing Detector
papers.abstract: The High Granularity Timing Detector (HGTD) currently in the production phase will mainly mitigate the pile-up effect in the ATLAS forward region and serve for bunch-by-bunch luminosity measurements in the high-luminosity (HL) phase of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). The HGTD utilizes Low Gain Avalanche Detector (LGAD) technology, covering the pseudorapidity range between 2.4 and 4.0, and provides high-precision timing information to distinguish collisions occurring close in space but well-separated in time. A pre-production batch of 8-inch silicon wafers was fabricated and a systematic quality control test campaign was carried out. This paper describes the Quality Control (QC) required for full-size (15 $\times$ 15 array) sensors, including leakage-current and breakdown measurements performed on all sensors at the vendor sites, as well as more detailed electrical characterizations at the participating ATLAS-HGTD institutes. In addition, the electrical characterization of full-size sensors after irradiation is reported.
authors: P. J. Dos Santos De Assis

papers.title: An Optimization Framework for Denoising Generation
papers.abstract: Noise-unconditioned denoising learns a single score, so generation can be viewed as gradient ascent on a fixed log-density landscape. This optimization interpretation leaves two questions: do trajectories approach meaningful data, and do different initializations retain diverse outcomes? We establish both phenomena for empirical and population multi-scale Gaussian-mixture objectives. Under explicit posterior and landscape conditions, ascent converges almost surely within $O(mσ_{\min}^2/τ)$ of an $m$-dimensional reference manifold with reach at least $τ$. We derive a source--sink identity for the same fixed field and use it to prove finite-resolution regional coverage. In an affine construction, we further identify a positive-bandwidth regime where even empirical-score optimization can avoid training-sample memorization while preserving diversity at the training resolution. The same fixed objective naturally supports penalty-guided controllable generation. Experiments support our predicted mechanisms, show improved robustness under large-step guidance, and demonstrate downstream gains consistent with finite-data generative generalization.

papers.title: EGS: A Complementary Safety Framework for Educational LLMs
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer strong potential for personalized education, but adolescent-facing deployment raises risks of toxic, biased, misleading, or developmentally inappropriate content. We argue that educational safety should move beyond binary refusal: student queries are often ambiguous or curiosity-driven, requiring contextual guidance rather than simple blocking. We introduce the Educational Guardrail System (EGS), a lightweight, model-agnostic runtime framework that complements intrinsic alignment through query moderation, scenario-aware pedagogical guidance, and response moderation. EGS triages inputs by risk level, redirects gray-zone queries with category-specific educational interventions, and audits outputs before delivery. Experiments across general and education-specific benchmarks show that EGS improves moderation performance, refusal quality, and jailbreak robustness across diverse LLMs. These findings suggest that defense-in-depth guardrails can strengthen safety while preserving the pedagogical utility required in educational LLMs. Our code and model weights will be publicly available to support community adoption.

papers.title: Flocking Time and Graph Volume in Nonlinear Cucker-Smale Models with Dynamic Networks
papers.abstract: This study proposes a Cucker-Smale model incorporating dynamic networks and the discrete $p$-Laplacian ($p \in (1,2)$) and analyzes the relationship between flocking time constraints and graph connectivity from both theoretical and experimental perspectives. We establish that this model achieves flocking within finite time and derive a quantitative relationship between the lower bound of flocking time and graph volume. Based on these results, we observe that imposing sufficiently small flocking time induces an increase in network volume, and that larger initial velocity variance requires greater volume under the same time constraint. In our experiments, we trained a transformer-based PPO policy to select network structures at each time step. Under the most stringent time constraint, the maximum average number of connections increased sharply, confirming a threshold effect. The negative correlation between convergence time and average number of connections reflects the theoretical results well. This study provides quantitative evidence for the phenomenon that time constraints induce connection mobilization.

papers.title: More lower bounds for Hales--Jewett and van der Waerden numbers
papers.abstract: We give explicit colourings improving the comparison lower bounds assembled here for several Hales--Jewett and van der Waerden numbers. The main algebraic tool generalises Rabung's power-residue colouring from arithmetic progressions to arbitrary sets. If every translate of a t-element set S in F_p meets at least two classes of the r-th power character, and the integer weights have both parities, then a period-2p one-weight colouring of [t]^p has no monochromatic combinatorial line. The 19 displayed algebraic certificates comprise 18 improvements and one closed-form reproduction; they include HJ(4,3)>=164, HJ(5,4)>=7418, and HJ(5,6)>=34034. The underlying period-p construction also proves kappa_ow(t,r)>=p-1 for the one-weight bracket ceiling, in particular kappa_ow(5,4)>=7416 and kappa_ow(5,6)>=34032. Warm breakout-weighted tabu search on the type simplex gives HJ(3,4)>=51. Whole-colouring local search gives W(8,3)>522, W(11,3)>1193, and W(17,3)>3620. All accepted certificates are available separately and are checked by direct enumeration; unresolved searches are reported as UNKNOWN, not UNSAT.

papers.title: TAILROLL: Tail-Aware Rollout Acceleration for RL-Based LLM Post-Training
papers.abstract: RL post-training of large language models (LLMs) is bottlenecked by rollout: heavy-tailed responses leave engines idle as each step waits for the longest response. Asynchronous training masks, but does not eliminate, idle time. We distinguish imbalance waste (uneven placement and decode contention) from straggler waste (waiting for the longest response). Tail length, not average load, often sets the step bound. We propose TAILROLL, an online scheduler integrated into an open-source RL framework. It combines stateless in-flight migration and sufficiency-gated termination. Migration moves decoding requests between engines at chunk boundaries and resumes them with one re-prefill under a freeness-based, cost-aware tail-balancing policy. Termination stops a response when its GRPO group has enough completed samples for advantage estimation, masking its partial output from the training loss. Across ten configurations, TAILROLL reduces rollout bubble ratio by 21% to 74% and cross-engine KV-cache imbalance by 44% to 79%. In end-to-end RL training, it cuts rollout time by 24% to 34%, full step time by 21% to 22% on long-CoT RL, and p95 request latency by 28% to 37%, while raising generation throughput by up to 33% with comparable or higher final reward.

papers.title: ARG-Avatar: Animation-Rendering Guidance for Efficient Feedforward Avatar Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Reconstructing animatable 3D human avatars from images is important for applications such as gaming and augmented reality. Feedforward methods make avatar reconstruction accessible by reducing inference time to a few seconds, but recent approaches rely heavily on scaling model capacity, training data, and computation. We ask whether such scaling is necessary. To this end, we introduce ARG-Avatar, an efficient feedforward framework with only 68M trainable parameters that achieves SOTA reconstruction quality. Our key insight is that 3D animation and rendering already provide strong geometric correspondences that existing methods largely attempt to learn from data. In light of this, we design the Foreground Avatar Coordinate RoPE attention (FACRoPE) and Intermediate Token Rendering (ITR) pipeline to guide avatar tokens to attend to their corresponding patches. Experiments across multiple datasets show that ARG-Avatar consistently outperforms prior methods when using two or more input images. Compared with LHM++, ARG-Avatar uses approximately 9$\times$ fewer trainable parameters, 4.8$\times$ fewer training sequences, and 14$\times$ less training compute, while running 6$\times$ faster and achieving a 2.7 dB PSNR improvement on the out-of-distribution NeuMan benchmark.

papers.title: A Study of the PDE Model for the Anisotropic Consensus-Based Optimization
papers.abstract: We investigate the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation associated with anisotropic consensus-based optimization. Under suitable assumptions on the objective function, we establish global existence and uniqueness of density-valued weak solutions for bounded initial probability densities with finite fourth moment. The main analytical challenge arises from the component-wise degeneracy of the diffusion, which vanishes along moving coordinate hyperplanes determined by the weighted consensus point. To overcome this difficulty, we develop spatial translation estimates based on weighted gradient bounds and uniform density estimates. Combined with temporal translation and moment estimates, these yield strong compactness in $L^2((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ through the Fréchet--Kolmogorov compactness criterion, enabling passage to the limit in the regularized equations. Uniqueness is established through the associated McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and Wasserstein stability of the weighted consensus point. Furthermore, we prove the propagation of $H^2$-regularity for sufficiently regular initial data.

papers.title: Contact-number hyperuniformity at glass close packing in infinite dimensions
papers.abstract: We investigate contact-number fluctuations of harmonic spheres near glass close packing (GCP), the amorphous jamming endpoint reached by compressing an ideal glass. Using replica theory, we show that the Gardner-unstable region shrinks toward jamming as the spatial dimension increases, allowing GCP to be approached along a stable one-step replica symmetry breaking branch in the high-dimensional limit. By coupling an external field to the local contact number, we derive the variance of the total contact number and the wave-number-dependent structure factor directly from the microscopic interactions. At GCP, the structure factor vanishes quadratically at small scaled wave numbers, demonstrating contact-number hyperuniformity. Upon weak compression above GCP, the structure factor develops a low-wave-number plateau whose height is proportional to the excess coordination. These results provide an analytical description of contact-number hyperuniformity and its breakdown upon compression.

papers.title: Sample-efficient Personalization of Large Language Model Alignment with Multidimensional User Preference Data
papers.abstract: Preference alignment has become a central tool to align large language models (LLMs) with human values and desired behavior, and its online variant can further advance their capabilities beyond what static data alone offer by repeatedly generating and labeling new responses with human feedback. But costly, time-consuming annotations limit its scalability, making sample efficiency essential, and existing methods typically seek to improve it by expanding coverage of the response space or selecting pairs with the highest uncertainty for comparison. Although they are effective, these methods quantify uncertainty from the perspective of the LLM, which may differ from the uncertainty perceived by the user: a pair can appear highly uncertain to the LLM even when past comparisons from the user already imply a clear ordering. In this paper, we propose multidimensional preference-guided online direct preference optimization (MPG-DPO), which leverages low-cost multidimensional evaluations from automated verifiers on the user historical comparisons to construct a personalized preference cone guiding response selection for online preference alignment. Specifically, it first discards responses that are confidently dominated under the estimated user preference, then selects two responses that are competitive under the retained preference cone yet exhibit the strongest unresolved disagreement. Theoretical analysis shows that, with high probability, the fraction of queries spent on cone-dominated responses vanishes as learning progresses. Experiments across multiple LLM families show that MPG-DPO outperforms strong contenders under matched query budgets.

papers.title: Emergence and Persistence of Maximal Atom-Field Entanglement in the Jaynes-Cummings model
papers.abstract: We investigate the emergence and persistence of maximal entanglement between a two-level atom and a single-mode quantized electromagnetic field inside a cavity, whose dynamics are governed by the Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonian. Using the von Neumann entropy as a measure of entanglement, we establish a direct connection between entanglement, atomic coherence, and atomic population inversion. This establishment shows that maximal atom-field entanglement is achieved when both the atomic population inversion and the $l_1$-norm of atomic coherence simultaneously vanish. By considering the atom initially in its excited state, we further demonstrate that the persistence of maximal atom-field entanglement strongly depends on the initial state of the field. For field states whose photon-number distributions have no two consecutive occupied photon-number levels, the local atomic coherence remains zero throughout the evolution. Consequently, complete collapse of the atomic population inversion for an extended period leads to persistent maximal atom-field entanglement. In contrast, for other field states, the interaction generates local atomic coherence, resulting in transient maximal entanglement. Our results demonstrate how the choice of the initial field state controls the temporal characteristics of entanglement in the Jaynes-Cummings system. The generation and persistence of maximal atom-field entanglement in such systems could be valuable for applications in quantum information processing.

papers.title: Joint-ID: Transformer-based Joint Image Enhancement and Depth Estimation for Underwater Environments
papers.abstract: Underwater imaging is a challenging task due to factors such as scattering, absorption, and turbulence, which degrade image quality and limit visibility. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for enhancing underwater images that leverages the benefits of joint learning for simultaneous image enhancement and depth estimation. We introduce Joint-ID, a transformer-based neural network that can obtain high-perceptual image quality and depth information from raw underwater images. Our approach formulates a multi-modal objective function that addresses invalid depth, lack of sharpness, and image degradation based on color and local texture. We design an end-to-end training pipeline that enables joint restoration and depth estimation in a shared hierarchical feature space. Additionally, we propose a synthetic dataset with various distortions and scene depths for multi-task learning. We evaluate Joint-ID on synthetic and standard datasets, as well as real underwater images with diverse spectra and harsh turbidity, demonstrating its effectiveness for underwater image enhancement and depth estimation. Furthermore, we demonstrate the ability of Joint-ID to perform feature matching and saliency detection for visually guided underwater robots. Our proposed method has the potential to improve the visual perception of underwater environments and benefit applications such as oceanography and underwater robotics. Supplements are available at: https://sites.google.com/view/joint-id/home

papers.title: On continuous unitriangular matrices on \(\mathbb R^2\)
papers.abstract: Let \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\C)\) be the group of complex \(2\times 2\)-matrices with determinant \(1\). We prove that each continuous map \(A:\R^2\to\mathrm{SL}_2(\C)\) can be written in the form \[A=\begin{pmatrix}1&f_1\\0&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\f_2&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&f_3\\0&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\f_4&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&f_5\\0&1\end{pmatrix}, \] where \(f_1,\ldots,f_5:\R^2\to\C\) are continuous functions.

papers.title: The Nygaard graded piece, the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex and regularity criteria
papers.abstract: For a $p$-torsionfree $p$-quasisyntomic ring, we construct a fiber sequence relating the $p$-th Nygaard graded piece of absolute prismatic cohomology to the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex. The latter is an arithmetic analogue of the cotangent complex in which the differential of $p$ need not vanish. We also clarify the relationship between the regularity criterion proved by Mao using the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex and the regularity criterion established by Bhatt and Mathew using the Nygaard graded piece. This relationship was anticipated by Bhatt and Mathew.

papers.title: Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression
papers.abstract: Scaling has driven the success of large language models (LLM), with sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures enabling greater parameter capacity without a proportional increase in computation. At large scales, MoE models rely on expert parallelism to distribute experts across devices. Each MoE layer requires two synchronous collective communication steps during inference: dispatching hidden states to the activated experts and combining the resulting expert outputs. As compute throughput has outpaced interconnect bandwidth, these synchronous collectives have become a major bottleneck to MoE scaling and efficiency. We address this challenge with EchoMoE, a lightweight architecture modification that retrofits existing MoE models, requiring approximately 8,500x fewer training tokens than full pretraining. Motivated by the observation that transformer blocks update the residual stream incrementally, we use a hidden state from an earlier layer as a reference and communicate only the compressed difference between it and the current state, rather than communicating each hidden state in full. EchoMoE periodically refreshes these reference states and transmits only the compressed differences synchronously, reducing the traffic on latency-critical paths without significant computational overhead. EchoMoE reduces inter-node communication volume by 58% and improves throughput by 22.6%, while preserving average performance within 3.8 percentage points across 18 benchmarks. EchoMoE further improves inference throughput by up to 2.38x over bandwidth-constrained Ethernet, paving the way for wide-area distributed inference. EchoMoE also tolerates quantization of the communicated representations without measurable quality loss. We release an efficient implementation for applying EchoMoE to pretrained MoE models, together with an inference integration for vLLM.

papers.title: Settling the Time and Structural Complexity of Bertrand Networks
papers.abstract: In the seminal Bertrand network game introduced by Babaioff et al. (2013), each seller posts a single price to captive buyers and to the markets it shares with neighboring sellers, where sellers cannot price discriminate across the markets. Although the existence of equilibria and polynomial-time algorithms to compute them in trees (Babaioff et al. (2013)) have been known, it has been a major open problem whether there exist efficient algorithms to compute them for general graphs. In this paper, we resolve this open question negatively by proving that computing any constant-error approximate Nash equilibrium in a Bertrand network is $\PPAD$-complete. This hardness holds even on sparse bipartite graphs of maximum degree five with constant integer market weights. Complementing our hardness result, we design an efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme (EPTAS) when both the maximum degree and the number of sellers with captive buyers are bounded. Beyond time complexity, since exact equilibria require randomizing prices over continuous intervals, another fundamental question left open by Babaioff et al. (2013) is whether an exact equilibrium can always be represented with a finite number of price intervals, \ie whether its structural complexity is finite. We resolve this question affirmatively by proving that every achievable equilibrium revenue profile can be realized by an equilibrium with structural complexity $O(2^n)$, which leads to an exact algorithm running in doubly exponential time. We further show that this bound is tight: there exist instances for which the unique equilibrium realizing target revenue profiles has structural complexity $Ω(2^n)$.

papers.title: An Explicit Parallelizable Robin-Robin Splitting Scheme for Navier-Stokes-Naghdi Shell Interaction
papers.abstract: We develop a novel explicit Robin-Robin splitting scheme for the system of an incompressible viscous fluid coupled to a time dependent Naghdi shell model. The shell model includes three displacement components and three independent rotation components, accounting for membrane, bending, and transverse-shear deformations. Both Robin conditions depend only on interface data from the previous time step, allowing the fluid and shell subproblems to be solved independently without coupling subiterations. For the fixed-domain Stokes-Naghdi problem, we derive a discrete energy identity that incorporates shell rotational inertia, interface velocities, and interface loads. We prove that the scheme is unconditionally stable for any fixed positive common Robin coefficient under homogeneous external data. Under suitable regularity and initialization assumptions, we establish first-order consistency and an $O(\sqrt{Δt})$ temporal error bound in the mechanical energy norm. Numerical experiments with a moving-domain pressure pulse compare the proposed scheme with the kinematically coupled $β$-scheme and a monolithic solver. To demonstrate its applicability to a more realistic vascular configuration, we simulate a stented artery using a bonded layered shell with stiff strut bands, capturing spatial variations in the arterial wall response.

papers.title: Learning Optimal Transport Plans Via Autoregressive Token Regression
papers.abstract: Optimal Transport (OT) provides a principled framework for finding the minimum cost coupling between probability distributions. Classical solvers remain the gold standard for this task. At the same time, OT is an ideal testbed for studying whether learning-based amortized models can internalize the structure of OT type problems. Here, ground-truth solutions are available and marginal constraints are explicitly defined. Also, exact discrete solutions have well-characterized sparsity. We describe ToR-OT, a transformer-based model that learns to predict discrete OT plans through autoregressive token regression. We reframe OT into a structured sequence generation task. ToR-OT decodes sparse transport plans as sequences instead of solving an optimization task at test time. We focus on three properties: (a) Zero-shot generalization: pretraining on a large synthetic corpus of OT instances allows a single model to generalize to unseen distribution pairs and heterogeneous cost metrics without retraining, (b) Sparse primal decoding: by exploiting the inherent sparsity in exact discrete OT solutions, the decoder predicts only nonzero entries (avoids dense coupling outputs), (c) Amortized inference: on low-dimensional discrete problems, ToR-OT gives accurate approximate plans and compares favorably with per-instance neural OT baselines. Overall, ToR-OT is not yet a replacement for classical solvers, but a step toward understanding how autoregressive transformers can learn structure of constrained optimization problems like OT.

papers.title: Fine-Grained Japanese Clinical Named Entity Recognition: A Controlled Comparison of BERT and Open-Weight Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Background: Generative large language models (LLMs) offer an alternative to encoder-based clinical named entity recognition (NER), but their performance on fine-grained Japanese extraction tasks and sensitivity to generation settings remain uncertain. Methods: We compared two fine-tuned BERT-CRF baselines with nine open-weight LLMs on iCorpus, which defines 113 entity categories. The evaluation used 433 sentences from 36 test documents; 1,672 sentences were used for training. LLMs were evaluated using zero-shot prompting with and without JSON Schema constraints and three-seed QLoRA fine-tuning. Fine-tuned models were assessed under different output-token limits, including 900 and larger model-specific limits of 2,600 or 4,096 tokens. Performance was measured using sentence-level label-surface matching with relaxed and exact-surface F1. Results: The highest zero-shot relaxed F1 was 0.337, compared with 0.836-0.841 for the BERT baselines. At the larger output limits, all eight fine-tuned LLMs with at least 13B total parameters exceeded both BERT baselines (relaxed F1, 0.882-0.914; exact-surface F1, 0.840-0.880). Across three-seed means, increasing the output limit improved relaxed F1 by 0.052-0.085, alongside higher recall and fewer length-limited outputs. JSON Schema constraints changed relaxed F1 by -0.014 to +0.008 among seven models outside the two reasoning-oriented configurations, while medical-general model pairs showed no consistent advantage for medical specialization. Conclusions: On this historical Japanese case-report benchmark, task-specific fine-tuning combined with adequate generation capacity was associated with stronger LLM extraction performance. Output-token limits materially affected comparisons with BERT, whereas enforcing output structure alone did not overcome low zero-shot accuracy.

papers.title: Safely Mitigating Grid Imbalance: A Hybrid Distributional Wide-Margin Recourse Approach
papers.abstract: This paper proposes the Multi-Agent Distributional Wide-Margin Policy Gradient (MADWMPG) framework: a dual-policy hybrid imitation and safe reinforcement learning (IL-SRL) method designed for safely mitigating grid imbalance in multiphase active distribution networks with distributed soft open points (SOPs). The framework comprises a wide-margin constraint barrier recourse (WCBR) module that seeks the maximal separation of constraint-compliant and unsafe actions and learns to proactively suppress exploratory violations. The framework addresses operational volatility using a novel adaptation of noncrossing quantile regression (NQR) distributional critics that track the complete distribution of policy returns. The set of behavior and recourse policies integrates an instantaneous physics-based and differentiable action projection mechanism that generates SOP constraint-compliant actions without relying on active learning. Policy safety is made responsive using an enhancement of conventional experience replay, and the safety performance of the framework is supported by probabilistic bounds derived in the paper. The proposed framework was trained and tested on a modified multiphase IEEE 123-bus test feeder. Results demonstrate its superiority to conventional reinforcement learning and SRL methods and show that it is highly competitive against the nonlinear AC optimal power flow.

papers.title: Subsystem Stabilizer $(r,δ)$-Locally Recoverable Codes: Characterization, Bounds and Constructions
papers.abstract: Local erasure recovery limits the number of physical systems accessed to repair a distributed quantum memory. For subsystem stabilizer codes (SSCs), a basic question is whether erasures can be corrected within a prescribed repair set. In this paper, we study subsystem stabilizer $(r,δ)$-locally recoverable codes ($(r,δ)$-SSLRCs), in which each coordinate belongs to a repair set of size between $δ$ and $r+δ-1$ that corrects any set of up to $δ-1$ erasures while preserving the logical subsystem and allowing the gauge subsystem to change. We first characterize local erasure recovery algebraically and apply this criterion to Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) and Hermitian hull constructions for $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs. For $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs, without assuming purity, we derive a redundancy bound for disjoint repair sets, a supported-subspace bound based on supported stabilizer and gauge subspaces, and a mixed counting bound for known erasures within selected repair sets and errors at unknown positions outside their union. For pure $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs with overlapping repair sets, we establish the Singleton-type and alphabet-dependent bounds, together with explicit Griesmer, Hamming, and Plotkin bounds. Moreover, we construct nine classes of $\F_q$-linear pure $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs from maximum distance separable (MDS) stabilizer codes, Reed-Solomon (RS) codes, and linear codes with MDS Hermitian hulls, which are simultaneously optimal with respect to several bounds for $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs.
